page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage but is Premium Storage capable, and contains no GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. The CPU achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as PassMark CPU, encryption, and physics evaluations. Memory performance is similarly strong, with read-only small block bandwidth and large block write bandwidth both ranking in the top 10%. Database operations, measured via PassMark and Redis SET operations, also place in the top tier.

While the instance excels in memory-intensive tasks and CPU-bound calculations, it exhibits moderate performance in large-scale LLM inference, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the middle 50% tier. The absence of local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive database workloads, large-scale caching layers, data decompression tasks, and enterprise-grade web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 96 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high-density 8.0 GB per core memory profile. The instance lacks local storage but supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks place this server in the top 10% for single-core and multi-core CPU execution, memory write bandwidth, and database operations, including Redis SET performance. However, large-scale LLM inference represents a relative bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing scoring in the average tier. This hardware configuration is highly efficient for memory-intensive database hosting, high-throughput caching, and complex enterprise workloads requiring substantial RAM capacity without dedicated GPU acceleration.
